chunks: That which the Sheikh — may God the Exalted strengthen him — informed me. He said: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Abu Usama, who said:
I asked Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about vomiting — does it break the wudu? He said: 'No.'

key_terms.اَلْقَيْءِ: vomiting (al-qay') — the regurgitation of stomach contents; the subject of the jurisprudential query in this hadith
key_terms.اَلْوُضُوءَ: wudu — the minor ritual ablution required before salat, touching the Quran, and other acts of worship
key_terms.يَنْقُضُ: breaks/invalidates (yanqudu) — to nullify an established state of ritual purity; the central legal verb of this ruling

ai.seo_question: Does vomiting (al-qay') break wudu according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Abu Usama questions Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) on whether vomiting (al-qay') nullifies the wudu, and the Imam delivers a succinct negative ruling. This is a defining Shia jurisprudential position: vomiting — regardless of quantity — is not among the ritual nullifiers (nawaqid) of wudu, contrasting with the Hanafi school which considers vomiting a mouthful to be a nullifier.
